summary: Sanitizes a string into an output buffer with a size budget. Returns 0 when either the input a1 or output a2 is null; otherwise clears the first output byte (this+0x0), and if the input is non-empty walks it with sub_5687F0 as the per-character 'needs encoding' test. Plain characters pass straight through via ASCIICharCodeValidation. A '+' (43) triggers special handling: if StringPrefixPatternCheck recognizes an existing '+~XX' escape, the 4-byte escape body is copied verbatim; otherwise the '+' is copied as a literal character. Characters are appended only while strlen(a2) stays under the a3 budget. When a character needs encoding, StringFormatWithBufferOverflowCheck formats it as the hex escape '%c%c%x%x' with prefix '+' (43) and '~' (126) plus the high and low nibbles, then appends. Returns 1 at end of input.

local_names.a2: output buffer receiving the sanitized text (first byte cleared to 0)
local_names.v6: second byte of an escape sequence after '+'
local_names.v13: single-character staging buffer for plain or encoded characters
local_names.v14: escape byte copied after the leading '+'
local_names.v15: escape byte copied after the second char
local_names.v16: escape byte copied after the third char
local_names.v17: null terminator byte of the escape staging

operations.description: If a1 or a2 is null, return 0
Clear the first byte of the output buffer this+0x0 to 0 before writing
If the input is non-empty, iterate while sub_5687F0 reports the current character needs no encoding
If ASCIICharCodeValidation accepts the current character, stage it verbatim for output
If the character is not '+' (43), stop the copy loop so the encoding path handles it

On a '+' (43): if StringPrefixPatternCheck recognizes an existing '+~XX' escape at the cursor, stage the 4 following bytes (v13, v14, v15, v16) verbatim and advance the cursor; otherwise treat the '+' as a literal character
Append the staged text with strcat only while strlen(a2) plus the staged length stays below the a3 budget
Advance the input cursor; return 1 when the null terminator is reached

When encoding is required, StringFormatWithBufferOverflowCheck renders the character into the staging buffer as '%c%c%x%x' with '+' (43), '~' (126), the high nibble and the low nibble, then the result is appended on the next pass
Invoked by settings, path and file-IO paths including SettingsCopySetupFileCopy, ConfigFileParser, PathBuilderWithBackslash, TextFileReader and AudioStreamOpen

clean_pseudocode: if (StringPrefixPatternCheck(v3)) { stage 4 escape bytes from v3; advance v3; }
unresolved: sub_5687F0 and StringPrefixPatternCheck define the character classification and the escape-prefix grammar, but neither is defined in this packet
The exact '+~XX' prefix is DERIVED from the format string '%c%c%x%x' with literals 43 and 126, not confirmed by an independent source
The output buffer this+0x0 is treated as the start of a2; its real capacity is separate from the a3 budget and is not defined
